Theorem
[Existence and Uniqueness of Geodesics]

1. ch4:4.27

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary and $ abla $ a connection in $TM$. For every $p\in M$, $w\in T_pM$, and $t_0\in \mathbb R$, there are an open interval $I i t_0$ and a geodesic $\gamma \colon I o M$ such that \[ \gamma (t_0)=p, \qquad \gamma '(t_0)=w. \] Any two geodesics with these initial data agree on their common domain.

Proof

\sketch In coordinates near $p$, introduce $v^i=\dot x^i$ and rewrite (4.16) as

egin{align} \dot x^k(t)& =v^k(t),\ \dot v^k(t)& =-v^i(t)v^j(t)\Gamma ^k_{ij}(x(t)). ag {4.17} \end{align}

This is the integral-curve equation for

egin{equation} G_{(x,v)}=v^k rac{\partial }{\partial x^k} igg|_{(x,v)} -v^iv^j\Gamma ^k_{ij}(x) rac{\partial }{\partial v^k} igg|_{(x,v)}. ag {4.18} \end{equation}

Local flow existence and uniqueness for $G$ give the required geodesic and local uniqueness. For two solutions, the set of times at which their positions and velocities agree is nonempty and locally open by the same coordinate argument; continuity makes it closed in the common interval. Connectedness of the interval gives equality on the full common domain.

□

A geodesic is maximal if it has no extension to a strictly larger interval. A geodesic segment has compact interval domain.
